core.title: Declare execution_kind on every acceptance, separate from harness/category
core.given: You author or edit an acceptance, selecting harness code/type and category as usual.
core.when: You classify the runtime environment it runs against.
core.then: Add execution_kind as a separate axis: hermetic_integration (real subject, boundary shape and integration sequence, no live external infrastructure) or live_smoke (verified against real live HTTP, DB, auth or deployment).
prefer: Select harness/category exactly as before, then add execution_kind.
hermetic_integration when the real integration runs without live infrastructure.
live_smoke when confidence comes from live infrastructure; SMOKE stays the live-infrastructure tier.
avoid: Encoding runtime environment in harness codes/types or category, or changing those enums.
Marking hermetic_integration an acceptance that calls live infrastructure.
Fakes (cassettes, recorded LLM responses) in hermetic_integration without a declared fidelity contract.
Treating hermetic_integration as a substitute for SMOKE's live confidence.
core.why: Live vs hermetic is a different question from harness or category; a separate axis keeps those enums stable while making live-infrastructure dependence explicit.
evidence: Every new or edited acceptance carries an execution_kind with value hermetic_integration or live_smoke.
harness_codes/harness_types/category values are drawn from the unchanged enums.
Acceptances marked hermetic_integration reference no live external infrastructure; any fakes they use have a declared fidelity contract.
Acceptances marked live_smoke verify against real live HTTP, DB, auth or deployment.
verification: The runtime-environment classifier execution_kind is an enum with exactly two values, hermetic_integration and live_smoke, and every new or edited acceptance declaration carries one.

execution_kind is orthogonal to harness_codes, harness_types and category; those enums are unchanged and must not be validated against execution_kind (the exclusion is only cross-validation of these axes against execution_kind; it does not lift the requirement that harness/category values come from their unchanged enums).

hermetic_integration means real subject, real boundary shape, real integration sequence and NO live external infrastructure; fakes (cassettes, recorded LLM responses) are permitted only with a declared fidelity contract, detailed in the sibling convention planner.acceptance.hermetic-fake-contract.
live_smoke means verification against real live infrastructure (HTTP, DB, auth, deployment); SMOKE remains the live-infrastructure confidence tier.
Term definition: execution_kind = the runtime-environment classifier for an acceptance.

Activation semantics carried from the reference: acceptance file_kind jointly with a create/edit operation is the required trigger, independent of whether execution_kind is already present or correct; a planner task that produces or revises acceptances is an alternative task-level trigger that fires even before a file diff exists; the change refinements (diff/schema observer reading execution_kind and harness/category fields) only target the check and never gate activation; a review finding (execution_kind missing, inconsistent with what the acceptance touches, or hermetic_integration fakes without a declared fidelity contract) optionally re-fires the rule on an otherwise untouched acceptance, and deciding whether verification touches live infrastructure needs judgment of the acceptance text.

values: new acceptance added (with or without execution_kind)
existing acceptance edited while lacking execution_kind
execution_kind inconsistent with what the acceptance touches (live infra vs hermetic)
hermetic_integration acceptance uses fakes without a declared fidelity contract

fires: Planner authors a new acceptance, whether or not it already declares a correct execution_kind.
Planner edits an existing acceptance that lacks an execution_kind.
Planner (re)selects harness code/type or category on an acceptance.
An acceptance verifies against a live deployment, database, auth provider or HTTP endpoint and must be classified.
An acceptance uses recorded LLM responses or cassettes instead of live infrastructure and must be classified.
A review finding reports an acceptance whose execution_kind is missing or inconsistent with what it touches.
doesNotFire: Editing plan or wagon prose that does not create or change an acceptance.
Code changes by a coder that do not touch acceptance definitions.

neutralityNotes: This convention is already stack-neutral: it governs planner-authored acceptance declarations and their schema (execution_kind, harness_codes, harness_types, category, the SMOKE tier, fakes such as cassettes and recorded LLM responses), all of which are defined by the ATDD convention set itself and are identical in every realization. No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path appears in any agent-facing item, so the core carries them verbatim, bunOnly is empty, and no profile keys are needed (a realization binds the 'acceptance' file kind and its plan/wagon topology to its own profile, but stating this obligation requires no such value). The sibling reference planner.acceptance.hermetic-fake-contract is a convention-namespace id shared across realizations, hence kept in core.verification rather than bunOnly. 'planner', 'coder', 'wagon', 'SMOKE' and 'cassettes' are ATDD methodology vocabulary, not stack terms. The Bun activation facts' REQUIRED/ALTERNATIVE/OPTIONAL notes have no slot in the core fact schema and are preserved in full in the activation-semantics entry of core.verification. The verifier exclusion in verifier_detail[1] is kept exactly as scoped in Bun: only cross-validation of harness/category against execution_kind is out of this check's scope, while the unchanged-enums requirement (evidence[1]) remains in force; no blanket harness/category-validation exemption is stated. unless is empty in both Bun and core, so it has no items to classify.
